scope: Backlog 2 Batch 025 — fixed membership S5323, S4778, S4629, S3407, S3996 only
model: GPT-5 Codex (medium); the workflow-default GPT-5.5 was not exposed in this workspace.

sourceCoverage.S5323: Attached 70-page primary PDF: article header/abstract, methods, Figures 1-5, Tables 1-8, results, discussion, limitations, references, and appended supplementary material scanned once. Direct extraction uses the primary 12-month injury-surveillance results in Tables 1-2; model-performance and cost tables are not outcome extraction data.
sourceCoverage.S4778: Attached primary PDF pp. 1-8: abstract, methods, Tables 1-3, results, discussion, limitations, and references scanned once.
sourceCoverage.S4629: Attached primary PDF pp. 1-7: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables 1-6, results, discussion, limitations, and references scanned once.
sourceCoverage.S3407: Attached 41-page primary PDF: abstract, methods, participant flow, Tables 1-6, Figure 2, results, discussion, limitations, and references scanned once. Figure 2 was visually checked; its 95-injury percentage denominator supports only the stated contact/non-contact count conversion.
sourceCoverage.S3996: Attached primary PDF pp. 1-10: abstract, methods/definitions, Tables I-III, Figures 1-2, results, discussion, limitations, and references scanned once. Supplementary Table I is cited for one-season results but was not embedded in the attached PDF.

checks: Each live primary PDF was downloaded and inspected once; its local SHA-256 was checked against the live primary-file SHA-256 before staging.

Population layouts were selected before field staging: Total for S5323; Total / 2010-2015 / 2016-2021 for S4778; Total / Training / Match for S4629; Total / Intervention / Control for S3407; and Intervention / Control for S3996.

Tabs 1-4 were checked for all five sources. Every reported results table and usable figure was swept for injury counts, rates, burden, severity, recurrence, mechanism/contact, diagnosis/type, location, and illness outcomes. No paper reports extractable illness outcomes.

No exposure, count, burden, or days-lost value was back-calculated from a rate. The only arithmetic is transparent source-row aggregation for compatible S3407 total structured counts and the Figure 2 contact/non-contact percentage-to-count exception using the printed total of 95 injuries.
S4778 is retained as eligible MLS injury-surveillance reporting under the workflow rule despite missing raw player-exposure totals.

studyDetails.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for non-contact injury prediction based on lower limb strength asymmetry in professional football
studyDetails.studyDesign: prospective cohort study [machine-learning model development and temporal validation]

participantCharacteristics.country: Europe (six top-tier clubs; countries not specified)
participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay: professional male football; six elite clubs in top-tier European leagues

definitions.injuryDefinition: time loss [non-contact tissue damage causing unavailability for football training or match participation]
definitions.severityDefinition: minimal 1-3 days; mild 4-7 days; moderate 8-28 days; severe >28 days
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: recurrent injury after an index injury; source does not provide a same-site rule
definitions.mechanismReporting: club medical staff using a web-based UEFA-methodology surveillance system; weekly data-completeness audits

caveats: The attached primary source is an accepted-manuscript version with 70 pages, including supplemental material. It identifies six European clubs but does not name the countries or print aggregate player-hour exposure totals.

The Table 2 component injury-type rows and the prose tissue-family percentages are internally inconsistent. Only the directly printed hamstring diagnosis row and compatible direct location rows are staged; no disputed parent-tissue aggregation is forced.
All recorded outcome events are non-contact lower-extremity injuries by the study definition; no illness data are reported.

studyDetails.title: ACL Injuries in Major League Soccer: A 10-Year Analysis of Injury Rate and Return to Play, and Performance Metrics by Player Position
studyDetails.studyDesign: retrospective cohort study of Major League Soccer Injury Surveillance database data

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [complete ACL rupture, with possible additional co-ligament involvement]
definitions.incidenceDefinition: annual ACL-injury rate reported by MLS Injury Surveillance database; raw player-exposure denominator not reported
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: subsequent ACL injury/reinjury as reported by the surveillance database
definitions.mechanismReporting: Major League Soccer Injury Surveillance database

caveats: MLS injury-surveillance reporting is eligible under the workflow rule. The authors explicitly note that their annual injury-rate calculation lacks individual player exposure, so raw exposure was not reconstructed.
The 47 contact and 69 non-contact values are direct Table 1 subsets whose sum is below the 144 tears because injury-onset data are incomplete; no missing mechanism is inferred.
Return-to-play and games-missed summaries are not recast as standardized time-loss severity fields.

studyDetails.title: Epidemiology of Sport Injury Among Korean Male Youth Soccer Players: A Prospective Cohort Study

definitions.injuryDefinition: physical complaint [any complaint arising during football; time-loss and medical-attention injuries included]
definitions.severityDefinition: slight 0 days; minimal 1-3 days; mild 4-7 days; moderate 8-28 days; severe >28 days
definitions.recurrenceDefinition: same body location and injury type after return to full football participation
definitions.mechanismReporting: certified athletic trainers; exposure collected by coaching staff

caveats: The Total / Training / Match layout preserves Table 3's directly reported outcome axis; all detailed type and location rows are pooled Total-only because the source does not give their training/match split.

The source prints only mean exposure per player, so aggregate player-hour exposure is not back-calculated. Its training-burden CI is preserved exactly as printed (`25.54-4.97`), although its reversed range needs reviewer attention.

Bone parent values and Hand parent values are transparent sums of directly reported compatible subrows. Contact (57) is the sum of other-player, moving-object, and stagnant-object contact rows; CIs and mean severity values are not aggregated.

studyDetails.title: One exercise session a day keeps the physio away: effect of a newly designed daily exercise programme on injury prevention in youth football - A randomised controlled trial

definitions.injuryDefinition: time loss [physical complaint preventing full participation in subsequent football training or match play]
definitions.severityDefinition: slight 0 days; minimal 1-3 days; mild 4-7 days; moderate 8-28 days; severe >28 days
definitions.mechanismReporting: academy physiotherapist using a standardized online injury-recording platform

caveats: The Total / Intervention / Control layout preserves the RCT comparison. Total structured rows and most-common summaries are transparent sums of the two Table 5 groups; no rates, burden, or severity values were summed.

Table 4's non-match category is not treated as training because the methods allow another occasion. Figure 2's contact and non-contact percentages were converted to 39 and 56 using its printed 95-injury denominator; the count conversion is the only percentage-derived value.
Table 5's Joint and Disc labels have no clean one-to-one schema field, and Sternum/ribs/upper-back is retained only in the compatible Trunk parent; no illness outcomes are reported.

studyDetails.title: Effect of the FIFA 11+ on anterior cruciate ligament injury incidence rates in collegiate female football players over three consecutive seasons
studyDetails.journal: The Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness

participantCharacteristics.levelOfPlay: collegiate Kanto University Women's Football Association Division 1

definitions.injuryDefinition: medical attention [MRI-diagnosed ACL injury occurring during football practice or match]
definitions.mechanismReporting: team athletic trainers or physiotherapists; ACL diagnosis by orthopedic surgeons using MRI

caveats: The Intervention / Control rows use Table II's all-player three-season player-season groups (389 / 343), not the smaller continuing-three-season subgroup (66 / 62).

Raw player-hour totals are not printed and were not back-calculated. Table III reports only non-contact playing-situation rows, so its training/match values are not inserted as total ACL match/training fields.
The source does not report illness outcomes, anatomical rows beyond the ACL knee diagnosis, recurrence, or standardized time-loss severity.
